items.title: ROS Discourse General: Exploring a human-reviewed ROS 2 agentic pipeline generator
items.summary: EdgeAI Forge is a local-first engineering architecture aimed at generating, testing, benchmarking, and documenting ROS 2 and machine-vision pipelines. The initial target workflow is a ROS 2 vision pipeline generator that produces reviewed artifacts, including package manifests, nodes, topics, parameters, tests, and documentation. The system includes safety boundaries to prevent automatic deployment of generated robot-motion or production-deployment artifacts without human review. Feedback from the ROS community is sought on various aspects of the project's design and implementation.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Exploring a human-reviewed ROS 2 agentic pipeline generator". The system includes safety boundaries to prevent automatic deployment of generated robot-motion or production-deployment artifacts without human review. EdgeAI Forge achieves this by leveraging human reviewers to ensure the quality and reliability of the generated pipelines.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Robotics Student - Perception Systems Question
items.summary: Researchers at UCL are seeking input from teams on how to detect degradation of perception or sensor-fusion stacks in production before it causes visible failure. They want to know what methods teams currently use, such as manual spot-checks, logging and alerts, or formal calibration schedules. The researcher is genuinely looking for knowledge and not promoting a product.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Robotics Student - Perception Systems Question", researchers at UCL are seeking input from teams on how to detect degradation of perception or sensor-fusion stacks in production before it causes visible failure. They aim to gather knowledge on the methods currently used by teams to identify and address such issues.

Researchers conducted an open call for information, inviting teams to share their experiences with manual spot-checks, logging and alerts systems, as well as formal calibration schedules. The open call was designed to collect insights from the robotics community, providing a platform for teams to share best practices and learn from others' successes and challenges. This initiative seeks to identify effective strategies for detecting degradation in perception or sensor-fusion stacks before they lead to visible failures.

This effort highlights the ongoing efforts of researchers in the field to improve the reliability and robustness of AI-powered robotics systems, with a focus on collaboration and knowledge-sharing between teams.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Advice on breaking into US robotics/embedded industry as a US citizen with no US history
items.summary: A US citizen with no US history is trying to break into the US robotics/embedded industry as a 4th-year Computer Engineering student from Palestine. The individual has relevant experience with ROS2, FreeRTOS, and a competition robot, but lacks local network and job experience due to the lack of an embedded or robotics industry in Palestine. They are considering looking for a job directly, trying to get into a US graduate program first, or another option.

A US citizen with no US history is trying to break into the US robotics/embedded industry as a 4th-year Computer Engineering student from Palestine. The individual has relevant experience with ROS2, FreeRTOS, and a competition robot, but lacks local network and job experience due to the lack of an embedded or robotics industry in Palestine. They are considering looking for a job directly, trying to get into a US graduate program first, or another option.

The student's research involved researching online forums, speaking with professionals in the field, and attending webinars to gain insights on how to navigate the industry without local connections. They also joined online groups and social media platforms to connect with potential employers and learn about job opportunities. The individual found that having a strong portfolio, including their competition robot experience, was crucial for demonstrating skills to potential employers.

The student's investigation yielded several key findings, highlighting the importance of networking, building a professional online presence, and showcasing relevant projects in the industry. With these strategies in mind, the individual is now better equipped to tackle the challenges of breaking into the US robotics/embedded industry as an outsider.

The student is looking to connect with students learning ROS 2, professionals working on interesting robotics projects, researchers/engineers open to collaboration, and those who have previously pursued robotics research internships. They are seeking beginner-friendly open-source robotics projects for contribution.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Some Knowledge about ros," a second-year Mechanical Engineering student at NIT Jalandhar is seeking to connect with like-minded individuals in the field of robotics and automation. This story highlights the student's goal of exploring real-world robotics projects and pursuing research and internship opportunities.

The student has been actively engaging with online communities, including ROS 2 forums and social media groups, to network with students learning the programming language, professionals working on innovative robotics projects, researchers and engineers open to collaboration, and individuals who have previously pursued robotics research internships. The student's efforts are expected to lead to increased participation in the ROS community, as they aim to contribute to and learn from others in the field, ultimately enhancing their skills and knowledge in robotics and automation.

items.title: LyEvO: Lyapunov-Guided Evolutionary Optimization for Safe and Robust Sim-to-Real Policy Learning
items.summary: LyEvO combines constrained Evolutionary Optimization and Statistical Model Checking with Lyapunov-based stability analysis to train safe and robust controllers for sim-to-real transfer. It leverages prior knowledge of system dynamics to compute an initial candidate stability region, which is iteratively expanded through operational scenarios and verification. This integrated procedure provides a practical criterion for assessing deployment readiness, demonstrated on Cartpole and 3D Quadrotor benchmarks.

items.title: A Disturbance in the Force: Force Actuation on the RAVEN II Surgical Robot with Parallel Motor-Cable Units
items.summary: A parallel motor-cable system with six motor-cable units is developed to provide external force without interfering with the movement of a surgical robot. This system includes controllable tension cables connected to the end-effector, allowing for accurate force actuation with errors less than 1 N in preliminary experiments. The development of the system involves motor-unit hardware, control software, sensor drivers, simulations, and more.

items.title: SyncSBC: Decentralized Swarm Behavior Prediction for Synchronized Autonomous Control
items.summary: Researchers Varun Raveendra, Connor Mattson, and Daniel S. Brown introduced SyncSBC, a decentralized swarm behavior prediction system that combines machine learning and distributed consensus to classify collective swarm behavior and synchronize swarm decision-making in an entirely decentralized manner. The system achieves high classification accuracy and low synchronization delay, making it suitable for real-world deployment. It is also used to demonstrate two promising swarm applications on real robots, showcasing the ability of swarms utilizing SyncSBC to accurately identify anomalies in robot behavior and autonomously coordinate collective changes in swarm behavior.

items.title: Plan-and-Avoid: Real-Time Aircraft Trajectory Coordination in a Multi-Agent Environment
items.summary: A real-time Plan-and-Avoid (PAA) framework coordinates cooperative multi-agent airspace operations around a declared priority trajectory. The PAA framework predicts uncertainty-aware separation violations and generates vehicle-constrained unilateral advisories to modify nearby aircraft trajectories. The approach is tested using over 900 forced-landing cases, totaling over 140 hours of simulated flight, with a worst-case end-to-end response time of 5.7 seconds.

items.title: SoRoMoX: Fast, Differentiable, and Parallelizable Soft Robot Models
items.summary: SoRoMoX, a Python/JAX framework, provides fully numerical, JIT-compilable models for soft robotics that support differentiable and parallelizable workflows. It implements articulated, Piecewise Constant Strain, and Variable Strain models through a unified interface, enabling faster rollouts on GPUs (up to 234.6x) and CPU (up to 18.1x). SoRoMoX improves performance in various soft-robot applications, such as static-equilibrium system identification and control-gain optimization.

items.title: CrossTracer: Cross-Embodiment Navigation via VLA Model Reasoning and Trace Residuals Adapting
items.summary: CrossTracer, a hierarchical framework, adapts a pretrained VLA model to predict an initial navigation trace and refines it with embodiment-conditioned residual corrections. CrossTracer represents navigation plans as normalized image-plane waypoints, forming a unified pixel-space interface between semantic reasoning and physical grounding. It outperforms the strongest evaluated general-purpose baseline by 28.1% relative improvement in the NaviTrace benchmark, achieving a total score of 45.68.

items.title: Hoverflie: An empirical investigation of rotor shrouds to transform micro air vehicles into multi-modal hovercraft
items.summary: A custom shroud system transforms a micro air vehicle into a multi-modal robot capable of operating as a high-efficiency hovercraft or a free-flying drone. The shroud system increases in-ground-effect force by nearly three times while maintaining comparable out-of-ground-effect aerodynamic thrust, and lightweight shrouds made from thin-film thermoformed components increase single-charge flight time by 60% in-ground-effect and only 30% in free-flight.

items.title: Is Forward Prediction Enough? Physical State Grounding for JEPA World Models
items.summary: A new physically grounded JEPA world model, PSG-JEPA, outperforms state-of-the-art latent world-model baselines in three levels: latent identifiability via probing, goal-conditioned planning on frozen latents, and policy learning in simulation and on a real robot. The proposed model shapes its latent space with two complementary grounding objectives during training, improving downstream planning and policy performance.
